One difference between the arms: whether the puzzle carried the two evidence lines.
Measured BEFORE the run: the answer is in the top-15 co-dependency list for 1.3% of obscure
reactions and in the top-15 co-expression list for 0.0%. If nothing moves, that is why.

DID THE SOLVER USE THE LINES AT ALL? it answered with a gene FROM the evidence 19/400 times
(18 of those were correct -- 94.7%, against 64.8% elsewhere).
A null with zero uptake would mean the lines were ignored; a null WITH uptake means they were
weighed and were not informative.
CONTROL ON THAT PRECISION -- did the NO-evidence arm already get those 19 rows?
base arm correct on the same rows        18/19
same gene named by BOTH arms             17/19
wins ATTRIBUTABLE to the evidence        0
So the high precision is not the evidence working. It is the chemistry working, on rows
where the list happened to contain the gene the solver was going to name anyway. A
convergence filter built on this would select nothing the model could not already do.
READING
NO EFFECT. Overall 0.645 -> 0.662 (+0.017, p=0.2962), obscure bin +0.050.
This was predicted by the retrieval measurement rather than discovered afterwards: evidence
that contains the answer for 1.3% of obscure reactions has almost nothing to add. Both
channels are LIVE -- they recover obligate complexes at rank 1 -- so the failure is about
WHAT THEY MEASURE. Co-dependency is viability covariance and co-expression is shared
transcriptional control; neither is a claim that one gene acts on another's substrate,
and most metabolic enzymes are non-essential in culture where the medium supplies the
pathway's product, leaving their profiles near-flat.
